R1C-bear-walk-0002.name: 850 m SW of Lee Lake
R1C-bear-walk-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R1C-bear-walk-0002.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2008 (18 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SE facing slope, 27 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 70 m E: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

seasonRows.notes: bag 2; Bow Only; no bow only season on the Gulf Islands in MU 1-1 (except Gabriola Island), in zone B of MU 1-5 (Map A12) or on Denman and Hornby Islands (MU 1-6)

plan: Drive: from District of Port Hardy, about 47 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 50.98219, -127.19161, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 350 m N, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 38 m, about 11 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 1-14, Region 1. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-08-24, closures 2026-10-16.
R1C-bear-walk-0002.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 1-14: about 6 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.00 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.3 km and about 38 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

R1C-duck-drive-0001.name: Burnett Lake
R1C-duck-drive-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R1C-duck-drive-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Burnett Lake, 39.2 ha, 80 m from the road.
About 6 wetlands within 2 km (estimate): ducks move between them.
Beside Kenneth River: backwater or oxbow (estimate).
Elevation 65 m: under 900 m, open water later in fall.

seasonRows.notes: District 1. Within the 8 a day: 4 northern pintails, 4 canvasbacks, 2 Barrow's or common goldeneyes together, 2 harlequins. Possession 24: 12, 12, 6, 6. Date for 2026 to 2027, worked out from the federal wording and matched to the BC synopsis (page 21 Region 1, page 28 Region 2). It moves each year.
